Dear Rep. Mano, I am a Salt Lake City resident (zip code 84105). I have an 8-year old daughter at Emerson Elementary who is not eligible for vaccination. Dear Council Member Mano, We write to request your strongest support for extending Mayor Mendenhall's K–12 mask mandate. Evidence shows that in these pandemic conditions, school mask requirements work. They keep kids safe; they keep kids in school; they keep parents working. On day 6 of school, our worst fears for the school year were realized when we received a close contact quarantine notice for our daughter from her first grade class at Emerson Elementary School. The boy who sits right next to her -- not even 3 feet apart, since the large class size and small classroom size don't permit it -- had tested positive for COVID. Dear Council Members, I am a parent in the Salt Lake City community. I know that you have heard from many parents regarding the mask mandate. I understand you are voting on this tomorrow. I am urging you to extend the mask mandate and I will briefly explain why. I am writing as a parent of a child with disabilities (down syndrome, sensory differences, and a challenged respiratory system since he was born with a congenital heart defect warranting surgery). My son's pediatrician made it very clear to us early on during this pandemic that our son is high risk if exposed to covid. He is also too young to be eligible to receive the vaccine. His health depends on the community around him to mask up. Children with various disabilities often have more complicated medical needs, relying on everyone around them to be extra responsible. Should the mask mandate go away right now, many families like mine would be in a horrible position, fearful to send their children to school since they are high-risk. Children like mine with documented disabilities and IEP's, especially need in-person education in order to meet learning goals. These include academic, social and behavioral goals often necessitating many specialists and therapists (speech, OT, PT, etc....) in order to learn and progress. These services are not "extra" and they often necessitate in-person learning. My child and all children with disabilities have a right to a safe, in-person education just like everyone else. For the people who are complaining about their freedoms being taken away when asked to mask, I propose another way to think about this---my child's right to an in-person education is undermined when those around him are not masking up. Essentially, his freedoms to attend school safely, learning like everyone else, could be at the detriment of his health. My son has a big sister, age 17 who is vaccinated and wears a mask to school every day. Should the mask mandate go away, her freedoms to attend school in person might be challenged because she could carry covid home to her brother if those around her aren't careful and wear masks. It is a community effort to protect ALL of our children. Removing the mask mandate at this time, prior to vaccine eligibility for the kids under age 12 especially as the Utah Covid case counts today have risen to over 4000 new cases, could be disastrous for many of these children with disabilities and their families. I urge you to continue the mask mandate in order to protect the rights and the health of my child along with many others like him. Thank you, Pamela Handman Pamela Geber Handman Professor, School of Dance University of Utah

Please vote to extend the emergency declaration and mask mandate for K12 SLC schools until the pandemic is controlled September 14, 2021 Dear Members of the Salt Lake City Council, I strongly support the mayor's local emergency declaration and mandatory masking in our K12 schools. Given the arbitrarily limited time frame for any executive order due to the state legislature's prior action, I ask that you take local legislative action to extend it. Instead of an arbitrary time limite, please tie its expiration to measurable public health milestones such as 90-95% vaccinated (staff, students, instructors) in the school system, level of community transmission (well below R0), and/or cases systemwide. COVID-19 doesn't care about dates, it cares about finding its next hosts and victims. My husband and I are childless by choice, so why do we care? Because we are community-minded, pay a disproportionate amount of our tax dollars into the school system compared to parents, and because what happens at school and at home doesn't stay at school or at home, especially in a pandemic. The Delta variant is the most transmissible one to date and spreads like wildfire. Breakthrough cases among we the "responsible vaccinated" are happening with increasing frequency. We are all in this together and must act in solidarity. My 7-year old nephew – in California, in a school district with strict COVID-19 rules and high community vaccination rates – already had to go home to quarantine due to an exposure at school the first week. Luckily, no one else tested positive – because of the strong measures taken at school. But his parents had to work from home or take time off to be with him during quarantine. We simply cannot have a functioning society and economy with a raging pandemic and large percentage of residents who refuse to comply with sensible and proven control measures - and often lie about it. As soon as the CDC released its misguided "the vaccinated can take off their masks policy" the obvious next thing happened – the radicalized unvaxed were happy to visibly lie about their status and go unmasked. That is why we need one consistent rule that all of us follow. The anti-masker anti-vaxers (and anti-science anti-evidence anti-critical thinkers) are ruining it for the rest of us. They must not be allowed to run rampant and perpetuate the pandemic. The rapidly increasing case loads and hospitalizations - most egregiously of children - show that this emergency is far from over. I also support this mandate for all Salt Lake City-controlled or contracted indoor venues and buildings and, if at all possible, for all licensed public business indoor areas, including common areas of the proliferating mid-rise multi-unit apartment complexes. At the beginning of the COVID-19 outbreak, science and epidemiology were scrambling to characterize and understand how this novel respiratory pathogen spread. A lack of understanding of science as a process and poor or misleading media stories led too many people to dismiss the now-proven value of masking as one of the key strategies against the spread of this deadly pathogen. (Note to school leaders - our education system is failing to teach science and critical thinking broadly enough in arguably the most technologically advanced era and nation.) Masking is especially valuable to protect those who cannot be vaccinated or whose immune systems are strongly compromised. It also helps protect the masses of people who have either been grossly misled by disinformation and are vaccine resistant or who have circumstances that so far have prevented them from getting vaccinated. Additionally, steps like better ventilation, social distancing and smaller class sizes, holding outdoor classes when possible, hybrid classes should continue into the future. This is a community-wide public health emergency that requires collective action. Masking is a minor inconvenience to save lives, prevent devastating and expensive illness and hospitalization. It also helps keep schools, the economy, and our fragile arts and restaurant/hospitality sectors afloat. It is part of the proven multi-pronged "swiss cheese" approach to controlling the spread of COVID-19. As some have quipped it's a minor inconvenience to wear a mask, but it is a major trauma to be intubated with failing lungs. Unfortunately, politicization of mask wearing – largely by an increasingly cynical and evidence-rejecting radical-right wing – has made this topic unnecessarily fraught. We need to call it for what it is – both-sides-ism is false in this pandemic. One major political party and ideology is actively undermining our ability to control the pandemic by deliberately taking away proven tools. What if they said that fire departments could no longer use ladder trucks, hoses, and fire hydrants? Or turnouts and breathing apparatus to enter burning buildings? That is basically what the supermajority Republican legislature has done. Its mindboggling. Please ignore the loud and selfish anti-maskers who are acting more like they belong to a cult than a civil society. The prison of their misguided belief system, honestly, is leading to more mass death than Jim Jones and the People's Temple, Marshall Applewhite and Bonnie Nettles and Heaven's Gate or other narcissist-driven pseudo-religious cults. In 2021, it is unbelievable that our county, state, and country are in this mess. Hundreds of thousands of deaths and millions of illnesses could have been prevented had we behaved better to this point. Countries that responded in a more unified, less politicized manner have done so much better than these United States, and especially Republican-led individual states. I had expected Utahns to rise to the occasion to save lives and protect children – to show how to do this well. Instead, a different social virus has infected far too many people, one that seems harder to combat, honestly. But we must try. There is no time like the present.
